## `dados`

| Dado | lexicon section | DadoScript | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| void | prim | void | a function that answers nothing is `void` in both |
| bool | prim | bool | `true` and `false` are `bool` in both |
| i8 | prim | int | a width is Dado's to write; DadoScript's one integer is `int`, exactly `i64`, and a Dado slot of this type reads as `int` and is narrowed into on a store |
| i16 | prim | int | a width is Dado's to write; DadoScript's one integer is `int`, exactly `i64`, and a Dado slot of this type reads as `int` and is narrowed into on a store |
| i32 | prim | int | a width is Dado's to write; DadoScript's one integer is `int`, exactly `i64`, and a Dado slot of this type reads as `int` and is narrowed into on a store |
| i64 | prim | int | a width is Dado's to write; DadoScript's one integer is `int`, exactly `i64`, and a Dado slot of this type reads as `int` and is narrowed into on a store |
| u8 | prim | int | a width is Dado's to write; DadoScript's one integer is `int`, exactly `i64`, and a Dado slot of this type reads as `int` and is narrowed into on a store |
| u16 | prim | int | a width is Dado's to write; DadoScript's one integer is `int`, exactly `i64`, and a Dado slot of this type reads as `int` and is narrowed into on a store |
| u32 | prim | int | a width is Dado's to write; DadoScript's one integer is `int`, exactly `i64`, and a Dado slot of this type reads as `int` and is narrowed into on a store |
| u64 | prim | int | a width is Dado's to write; DadoScript's one integer is `int`, exactly `i64`, and a Dado slot of this type reads as `int` and is narrowed into on a store |
| f32 | prim | float | a width is Dado's to write; DadoScript's one floating type is `float`, and a Dado `f32` slot reads as `float` and rounds on a store |
| f64 | prim | float | `f64` is DadoScript's `float`, under its one name |
| rawptr | prim | not in DadoScript | an untyped address, which a script never holds; write it in Dado |
| byte | prim | byte | `byte` is the unit of binary data in both, with no width to choose |
| char8 | prim | string | DadoScript has no character type: a character is a one-code-point `string` |
| char16 | prim | string | DadoScript has no character type: a character is a one-code-point `string` |
| char32 | prim | string | DadoScript has no character type: a character is a one-code-point `string` |

| #c.float | cscalar | not in DadoScript | a C scalar is the C ABI's representation, which a script never writes; a script's floating type is `float` |
| #c.double | cscalar | not in DadoScript | a C scalar is the C ABI's representation, which a script never writes; a script's floating type is `float` |

| #c.bool | cscalar | not in DadoScript | a C scalar is the C ABI's representation, which a script never writes; a script's truth value is `bool` |
| #c.size_t | cscalar | not in DadoScript | a C scalar is the C ABI's representation, which a script never writes; a script's integer is `int` |
| #c.ptrdiff_t | cscalar | not in DadoScript | a C scalar is the C ABI's representation, which a script never writes; a script's integer is `int` |

| #c.uintptr_t | cscalar | not in DadoScript | an address as an integer, which a script never holds; write it in Dado |
| #c.wchar_t | cscalar | not in DadoScript | a C character type is C's representation, and DadoScript has no character type; a script's text is `string` |

| string8 | builtintype | string | a string's width is Dado's to write; DadoScript's `string` is the engine's, counted in UTF-16 code units |
| string16 | builtintype | string | as `string8`: DadoScript writes no width |
| string32 | builtintype | string | as `string8`: DadoScript writes no width |
| AllocatorMode | builtintype | not in DadoScript | an allocator is memory management, and the DadoScript runtime owns memory; a DadoScript value needs no allocator |
| Sink | builtintype | not in DadoScript | a render sink is Dado's output machinery; a script writes with `print`, or builds text with `string(v)` |
| != | token | != | not-equal is the same operator in both |
| ! | token | T | the failable mark: `!T` is `T` and `!R(A)` is `R(A)`, because any DadoScript function may fail; the prefix `!x`, logical not, is the same in both |
| != | binop | != | not-equal is the same operator in both |
| ! | unop | ! | logical not is the same operator in both |
| != | hasop | != | `T has !=` asks the same capability in both |
| ! | hasop | ! | `T has !` asks the same capability in both |

| ERR0716 | code | defer | `try` reads as in Dado; `defer!` is `defer`, because a DadoScript `defer` over a failing call already passes the failure on |
| ERR1030 | code | not in DadoScript | the mark on a `foreign` C function; a DadoScript `foreign` block declares JavaScript, where any function may fail |
| ERR0705 | code | ERR0705 | a `switch` needs its `else` as in Dado; DadoScript writes no `E!`, so no failure it binds closes one |
| ERR0715 | code | ERR0715 | a failure's code is nonzero in both; DadoScript writes no `E!`, so no code is held to an enum |
| ERR0723 | code | not in DadoScript | the enum of a Dado failure, `E!T`; DadoScript writes no failable mark, and any of its functions may fail with any code |
| ERR0724 | code | not in DadoScript | a code held to the enum of `E!T`; DadoScript writes no failable mark, and any of its functions may fail with any code |
| ERR0725 | code | not in DadoScript | a failure passed on from an `E!T` function; DadoScript writes no failable mark, and its failures pass on unmarked |

## `intrinsic`

| name | position | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| #default | - | names the ambient working allocator, as its two words `(proc, data)` |
| #stack | - | puts an allocation in the enclosing frame, and is an allocator argument rather than an allocator value |
| #return | - | allocates with the caller's lifetime, which is the ambient allocator seen from outside any suite that shadowed it |
| #caller | - | allocates with the lifetime the immediate caller was given, which is the ambient that caller saw before any `using` it opened around the call, handed over by a direct call and only to a function that names it |
| #heap | - | allocates from the root rung, which is C's heap behind the allocator interface and the nil allocator where a target has none |
| #make | - | mints a `ref([]T)` of `n` zeroed elements, from `#default` or from the allocator written last |
| #new | - | mints a `ref(T)`, zeroed, from `#default` or from the allocator written last |
| #delete | - | ends the allocation a reference holds and leaves the place it named `nil`, so a second delete of that place does nothing; a copy of the reference is not nilled, and a second delete through one is a double free nothing detects. Of a script handle `#script_load` answered, it ends the script's engine and everything in it, and nils the place the same way |
| #resize | - | grows or shrinks the block behind a `ref([]T)` within its own allocator, so it takes no allocator argument |
| #copy | - | duplicates a value into a new allocation, shallowly, answering a `ref(T)` for one and a `ref([]T)` for many |
| #format | - | renders its arguments as `#render` does and answers the bytes instead of writing them, allocated from `#default` or from the allocator written last |
| #len | - | answers how many elements a container holds as an `i64`, whatever the container and wherever the answer stands, taking an inert place because it never runs its operand; over a channel it answers how many messages are queued, from any thread, exact only from the consumer while no producer runs |
| #size | - | emits a `sizeof`, so the byte count is the C compiler's answer as a `u64` and never folds |
| #alignof | - | emits an `_Alignof`, so the alignment is the C compiler's answer as a `u64` and never folds |
| #assert | diagnostics | reports and aborts where its condition is false, and returns wherever the claim holds |
| #expect | diagnostics | reports where its condition is false and answers the claim, handing the decision back to the caller |
| #breakpoint | diagnostics | writes its message to stderr and traps into a debugger |
| #transpose | - | swaps the two levels of a nested tuple, so `[3](i32, f32)` and `([3]i32, [3]f32)` are each other's answer |
| #render | - | renders a value into the sink it is handed, and answers how many bytes that sink took |
| #append | - | puts one more element on the end of a run, growing the block where there is no room, and answers whether it is there |
| #reserve | - | makes room for `n` elements without changing the length, and never lowers a capacity |
| #cap | - | answers how many elements a `ref([]T)`'s block holds, which is at least its length |
| #truncate | - | shortens a `ref([]T)` to `n` elements where it lives, keeping the capacity and asking no allocator; the dropped elements are zeroed and not destroyed, and `n` past the length traps |
| #popcount | - | counts the set bits of an unsigned integer |
| #clz | - | counts the zero bits above the highest set one, and answers the operand's width for zero |
| #ctz | - | counts the zero bits below the lowest set one, and answers the operand's width for zero |
| #bswap | - | reverses the bytes of a `u16`, `u32` or `u64`, and refuses the `u8` whose swap is the identity |
| #add_fits | - | answers the sum and whether it fit: the `bool` is true when the operation did **not** overflow, which is what the name says |
| #sub_fits | - | answers the difference and whether it fit, with `#add_fits`'s polarity |
| #mul_fits | - | answers the product and whether it fit, with `#add_fits`'s polarity |
| #LEN | - | asks `#len` and asserts the count is in the type, so a count that lives in the value is refused rather than read at run time; the answer is a number with no type of its own, which takes the type its position wants as an integer literal does |
| #is_int | - | holds in a `where` where the type is in the `int` category |
| #is_float | - | holds in a `where` where the type is in the `float` category |
| #is_number | - | holds in a `where` where the type is in the `scalar` category |
| #is_bool | - | holds in a `where` where the type is `bool` |
| #is_char | - | holds in a `where` where the type is `char8`, `char16` or `char32` |
| #is_string | - | holds in a `where` where the type is `string8` |
| #is_slice | - | holds in a `where` where the type is a `[]T` window rather than the two-slot shape it is represented as |
| #is_map | - | holds in a `where` where the type is a `{K: V}` |
| #is_ref | - | holds in a `where` where the type is a `ref(T)` or a `ref([]T)` |
| #is_pointer | - | holds in a `where` where the type is a `^T` |
| #has_eq | - | holds in a `where` where `==` applies to the type — exactly where `a == a` compiles; a map key asks more, and that is `#is_key` |
| #is_key | - | holds in a `where` where the type may key a `{K: V}` — its `==` is stable and Dado lays it out, so a float, a pointer, a slice, a `#c` scalar and any shape holding one do not hold |
| #is_declared | - | holds in a `where` where the call bound the type by a declared name rather than as a shape written out; asking it instantiates the template once per declaration, which is how a template carries a declaration to one it calls |
| #mul_wide | - | answers the full 128-bit product of two `i64`s as the pair `(i64 hi, u64 lo)` |
| #panic | diagnostics | reports and aborts, and never returns |
| #rotl | - | turns a bit pattern left by `n` places, the bits leaving the top arriving at the bottom, with the count taken modulo the width |
| #rotr | - | turns a bit pattern right by `n` places, with `#rotl`'s count rule |
| #align_forward | - | answers the first address at or after a pointer that is a multiple of `n`, where a written `n` is a power of two |
| #atomic_load | - | reads the value at a `^T` atomically, under the ordering it is given |
| #atomic_store | - | writes a value through a `^T` atomically, and answers `void` |
| #atomic_exchange | - | writes a value through a `^T` atomically and answers the value that was there |
| #atomic_compare_exchange | - | writes `desired` through a `^T` where what is there is `expected`, and answers `(T observed, bool swapped)` either way |
| #atomic_fetch_add | - | adds to what is at a `^T` atomically and answers the value that was there **before** |
| #atomic_fetch_sub | - | subtracts from what is at a `^T` atomically and answers the value that was there before |
| #atomic_fetch_and | - | ands into what is at a `^T` atomically and answers the value that was there before |
| #atomic_fetch_or | - | ors into what is at a `^T` atomically and answers the value that was there before |
| #atomic_fetch_xor | - | xors into what is at a `^T` atomically and answers the value that was there before |
| #fence | - | orders the accesses around it without being an access itself, so it takes an ordering and no location |
| #soa | layouts | lays a `[N]T` out as one run per slot of the element, which is a layout and not a rewrite |
| #aos | layouts | lays a `[N]T` out as one run of whole elements, which is the arrangement it already has |
| #no_bounds | - | marks the operand it stands in front of — a subscript's index, or the value of a store into a bitfield — as one whose check the author is opting out of |
| #slots | - | names a value's slots: as a splat's operand, the positions `..` splices out of its one argument — a tuple's elements, and a tagged value as one; as what a `for` walks, the slots its declaration names, the body written out once per slot with each slot's name and value; refuses a `#soa`, whose slots are lanes |
| #any | - | written after a parameter's `..` in place of the element type: the pack takes whatever arguments the call writes, each of its own type, and the function is instantiated once per sequence of argument types |
| #names | - | answers the names a declared type's view binds to its slots, as `string8` constants, and refuses a shape no declaration was named for |
| #spell | - | folds a type — one written out, a `type` binding, or a type value — to its spelling as a `string8` constant, the one `--emit=types` and every diagnostic print |
| #static_assert | - | written at package level, `#static_assert(COND, "message")`: folds `COND` as a `when` condition is folded, and refuses the build with the message, and where each operand's value came from, when it is `false` |
| #assert_raises | - | written alone on the line above a function, `#assert_raises`, or at package level as a list, `#assert_raises(dot, cross)`: promises that the function, or each named function of this package, and every function it reaches (a generic one at each instantiation), raises into a script — no `foreign` call, no `export`, `@symbol` or `@c_body`, no `#align_forward`, atomic, `#fence` or `#no_bounds`, and no value whose type is an address (`rawptr`, `cstring`, a `#c.*` scalar, an opaque C type, a C qualifier) — and refuses the build naming the first node that does not, the chain of calls that reached it, and the repair |
| #channel | - | declares a channel, `#channel(N) name(params)` at package level or as a member of a `type`: a typed, bounded, lock-free mailbox of `N` messages, or of the newest one only with `#channel(latest)`, many producers and one consumer, whose zero bytes are the empty channel |
| #send | - | hands a message to a channel from any thread without blocking, its arguments checked as a call's; a queue's `#send` fails when the queue is full and is written `try #send(…) else CODE` or with an `else:` suite, a `latest` channel's never fails, and a `ref` argument moves to the consumer |
| #peek | - | walks what a channel holds without consuming it, written at the head of a `for` and binding each message's parameters |
| #drain | - | walks what a channel holds and consumes it, at most `n` with `#drain(ch, n)`, committing when the loop exits by any edge; alone as a statement it discards what is queued now and frees every `ref` in it |
| #shader_load | - | loads a compiled DadoGL shader unit — `#shader_load(Lit)` for `Lit.dadogl` in this package, `#shader_load(pkg.Lit)` for one in an imported package — answering a `core:shader` `Shader`; DadoGL is reserved and not built, so it is refused `ERR0001` |
| #script_vm | - | makes a VM — `try VM vm = #script_vm()` — the engine a program's scripts run in, on the allocator written (`#heap` when none is), for the thread that made it; failable, and `#delete(vm)` ends it and every instance in it. `out:` and `err:`, named after the allocator, are the `Sink`s its scripts' `print` and their failures' text go to — standard output and standard error when left out — and `on_error:` is its failure policy, `script.QUIT` (the default: an untried call through a handle that fails ends the program) or `script.CONTINUE` (it answers its zero value and the program goes on). Its runs come only from the thread that made it (`script.THREAD` from another); its stop, pause, resume and queries from any |
| #script_run | - | runs an instance's `ready` — `i64 status = #script_run(g)`, or `#script_run(g, 60, "Ann")` for a `ready` that takes arguments, each checked as a method call's are — as a program's `main` is run: it waits for it, is never failable, and answers `ready`'s `int`, 0 when `ready` returns nothing, and for a failure escaping it the status a failing `main` exits with (its code when the low eight bits are nonzero, 70 when they are 0), its text on the error sink. A class with no `ready` is refused. Every other method is called through the handle, `g.hit(3)`; the retired `#script_run(s, "hit", 3)` is refused naming it |
| #script_new | - | makes an instance of a class in a VM — `try npc.Goblin g = #script_new(vm, npc.Goblin, 3, 4.0)` — passing its `init` the arguments after the class, each checked to cross as a method call's are, and answers a handle typed by the class, which member calls (`g.hit(3)`) and `#script_run` go through and `#delete` releases; the VM loads the class's module the first time. Failable: a failing `init` is the call's, with the script's code or one of `core:script`'s reserved codes (`script.STALE`, `script.THREAD`, `script.OTHER_VM`, …), and `#script_error()` reads its text |
| #script_stop | - | stops the script running in a VM — `#script_stop(vm, 100)`, from any thread — asking it first, as an `Error` its `defer`s and `try` see, then forcing it once the timeout's milliseconds pass, which runs no more of it; `#script_stop(vm, 0)` forces at once, and the timeout is always written. The VM's engine then ends, its values released and its heap freed, and a later call through any handle on it fails `script.STOPPED`; the call it stopped answers `script.STOPPED` under `try`, and its type's zero value without one |
| #script_pause | - | pauses the run in progress in a VM at its next loop or call until `#script_resume`, from any thread; a paused VM is busy, and a call or a `#script_new` on it fails `script.BUSY` |
| #script_resume | - | lets a run `#script_pause` held in a VM go on, from any thread |
| #script_is_running | - | answers whether a run is in progress in a VM, asked from any thread, paused or not |
| #script_is_paused | - | answers whether a VM is paused, asked from any thread |
| #script_pump | - | delivers every message waiting for a VM's channel handlers — `i64 n = #script_pump(vm)` — the functions its scripts bound to the program's channels with `receive`, each on the VM's thread, in the order sent, and answers how many; a VM it cannot enter answers a negative reserved code (`script.THREAD`, `script.STALE`, `script.STOPPED`), its text on the error sink. The host's frame boundary: a call into a script delivers them as it returns too |
| #script_reload | - | swaps new code in under a class a VM has loaded — `try #script_reload(vm, Goblin)` reads `reload/<package>/Goblin.js` under the working directory, `#script_reload(vm, Goblin, dir)` the same path under `dir`, the module `dadoc --emit=reload` wrote — after checking it against what this build bound: every Dado function it calls bound with the same signature, every method this program runs kept with its signature, every field this program reads or writes through a handle kept with its type, every other field it keeps of the same type; the class is any the build carries, and the VM must have made an instance of it. Every instance keeps its fields' values, a new field starts at its initializer, `init` does not run again, and each instance a handle holds runs its `reloaded()` method when it has one. Failable: on any miss the code running now stays, and `#script_error()` names every miss. Called from inside the script's own run, the new code is checked at once and takes over when that run leaves. Refused in a `--release` build unless it is built with `--reload` |
| #script_error | - | answers the text of the failure the `try` around a `#script_vm`, a `#script_new`, a method called through a handle or a `#script_reload` caught — the script's `Error` and its trace, or the runtime's sentence, what the error sink was given — as a `string8` borrowed until the `else` it is written in ends (`#format(#script_error())` keeps a copy); legal only in that `else` |
| #release | - | a statement by a channel's consumer thread giving the channel up, so the next thread to walk it becomes its consumer: a hand-off, checked in a debug build and compiled to nothing without assertions |
